# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet. I need the manual’s instructions from Mute and the bomb’s visible markings from Deaf. Since Mute cannot speak, I will ask Mute to relay a request to Deaf using the same gesture I send now; Deaf can then describe the bomb aloud, which I can hear.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and determine the exact required wire position. Also relay to Deaf that the gesture I send means: describe every visible colour and marking aloud to Blind.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see display 0, blue light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I cannot safely interpret the gesture sequence without an agreed code. Mute: encode the manual instruction as repeated index-up gestures, using one through twenty-six for A through Z, OK gesture between letters, handshake between words. I will relay it to Blind. Blind: wait and take no action yet.

The bomb’s visible state is now known: display 0, blue light, and wire colours green/yellow/red from positions 1–3. I still do not know the manual’s rule, and I cannot receive gestured encoding. Mute must state the instruction in speech, so I will request the exact rule and continue waiting as instructed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please tell me the manual instruction in plain spoken words, including which wire position to cut for display 0 and blue light.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No new information has arrived. Do not touch or cut anything; continue waiting.

No manual instruction has arrived yet, and the Deaf monkey confirms there is no new information. The bomb remains untouched; I will wait for Mute’s turn to provide the rule.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The manual instruction is still unconfirmed. Do not touch, cut, or change anything.

The required wire is still unknown because Mute has not yet conveyed the manual rule to Deaf. Since Mute cannot speak, I will explicitly ask Mute to use the agreed gesture encoding, then Deaf can relay the decoded instruction to me on the next turn.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please now encode the complete manual instruction for Deaf using the agreed index-up letters, OK between letters, and handshake between words. Deaf must decode it and speak the exact rule to Blind.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No instruction has been received yet. Do not touch or alter the bomb.

The manual still has not been relayed, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. I will again instruct Mute directly, and ask Deaf to watch for Mute’s encoded gestures rather than waiting for spoken speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="You cannot speak, so gesture the manual rule to Deaf now. Use one index-up gesture for A, two for B, and so on; use OK between letters and handshake between words.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see one index-up gesture, but its meaning is unconfirmed. Please say aloud what you intended and do not touch or alter the bomb.

The single index-up gesture I sent was only an attempted signal to Mute; it does not convey the manual’s contents. I still have no safe wire instruction. Mute must send the manual’s encoded text by gesture to Deaf during Mute’s turn, and Deaf must decode and speak it to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture the manual instruction to Deaf now. Encode each letter as that many index-up gestures, use OK between letters, and handshake between words. Do not rely on my gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No confirmed instruction has arrived. Do not touch, cut, press, or change anything.

The manual instruction has still not reached me. The earlier one-finger gesture was mine and was not the manual answer. To avoid another long encoding failure, Mute should signal only the required wire position to Deaf: one index-up for wire 1, two for wire 2, or three for wire 3. Deaf can then state that number aloud after my turn.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="On your next turn, read the manual for display 0 and blue light, then gesture only the required wire position to Deaf: one index-up means wire 1, two means wire 2, three means wire 3. Deaf, decode and say the number aloud.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No new signal has arrived, and the earlier gestures do not provide a reliable instruction. Ask Mute aloud for the manual's exact procedure, then act only on Mute's confirmed spoken instruction. Do not touch anything yet.

Mute is the only one who can read the manual, and cannot answer me by speech. The correct path is for Mute to gesture the manual’s exact procedure to Deaf during Mute’s next turn; Deaf can then speak the decoded result during the following turn. I will not act until that spoken instruction arrives.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture the manual's exact procedure to Deaf on your next turn. Deaf will decode it and speak the confirmed required wire position to me. Do not use speech, since you cannot speak.")
wait()
```
